note: Adversarial next-load scenarios not in conformance/fixtures/authority/grant-cases.json and never added to it (per contract, step 7). These record facts about what evaluate() and Cedar each do with a shape our declared corpus does not exercise: they are not a ruling on how Soveraeign should resolve conflicting grants.

scenarios.describes: Two RATIFIED grants cover the same actor and capability. The older grant admits services/ with no exclusion. The newer grant also admits services/ but excludes services/legacy/. A request targets services/legacy/thing.py.
scenarios.evaluate_reading: sovkernel.authority.evaluate() iterates the grant list in registry order and returns the verdict of the FIRST grant that covers the request (authority.py lines 187-192, `break` on the first `reason is None`). The older, unrestricted grant is checked first, covers the path, and evaluate() returns PERMITTED under grant:older-unrestricted without ever consulting the newer grant's exclusion.
scenarios.cedar_reading: Cedar authorizes against the whole policy set at once: a `forbid` fires the moment ANY policy's condition matches, independent of which entity or grant it names or how many other policies would separately permit. Modeled as one Path-scope forbid policy per grant's excluded_paths (see next-load.mjs), Cedar denies this request because the newer grant's exclusion fires, with no notion of grant order to resolve first.
scenarios.outcome_field: see next-load-results.json for the recorded Cedar decision

scenarios.describes: Issuer A grants actor B a capability; B in turn grants actor C the same capability (a delegation chain A -> B -> C); C makes the request.
scenarios.evaluate_reading: authority.py has no delegation concept at all: `_grant_unavailable` compares `grant.actor_id` to `request.actor_id` by string equality (line 95-96) and stops. Modeling a chain would need evaluate() to walk from the requesting actor back through however many `grant.issuer_id -> grant.actor_id` links exist, re-running every other check (status, revocation, time window, effect ceiling) at each link - a second loop nested inside the existing one, on the order of 15-20 new lines plus a cycle guard, none of which the corpus's single-hop grants exercise today.
scenarios.cedar_reading: A delegation chain is exactly what Cedar's entity hierarchy already expresses without new policy logic: give Actor C `parents: [Actor::B]` and Actor B `parents: [Actor::A]`, and a permit policy written as `principal in context.grant.actor` (rather than `principal == context.grant.actor`) authorizes any principal for whom the granted actor is an ancestor. The existing schema.Grant.actor attribute and the existing `in` operator already cover this; no new entity type or policy is needed, only changing one `==` to `in` in the one permit rule and adding `parents` edges when the entities are built.
scenarios.outcome_field: not executed - the point is expressible with the existing schema and a one-operator policy change, not a new run

scenarios.describes: A grant's scope admits services/ and excludes services/asset/src/legacy/quarantine/, three path segments below the admitted prefix.
scenarios.evaluate_reading: sovkernel.scope.out_of_scope() and _selects_excluded() (scope.py lines 117-159) already compare full normalised strings with `startswith`, so depth is free: `_selects_excluded` needs zero new lines for a deeper exclusion, and neither does out_of_scope's loop over `request.get('paths', ())`. Depth was never the axis that cost lines in this module; escape spelling was (D-008a through D-008l, each its own case).
scenarios.cedar_reading: Depth is likewise free once the Path entity hierarchy exists: the excluded entity `services/asset/src/legacy/quarantine` just needs `parents: [Path::"services/asset/src/legacy"]` (or directly `[Path::"services"]`, since `in` walks the full transitive closure regardless of how many entities sit between) and the existing `resource in context.grant.excludedPaths` forbid policy already reaches it. No new policy line either.
scenarios.outcome_field: not executed - both readings agree the fact is free in whichever direction the corpus's own D-007/D-008 pairs already cover; nothing here would be a new observation
